key_insight: SHOW3D introduces a marker-less, multi-camera capture system that records 3D hand and object interactions in unconstrained, real-world (egocentric) settings, producing high-quality 3D reconstructions and annotations outside studio environments. This bridges the gap between controlled datasets and real-world generalization for hand-object understanding.
problem_solved: Existing hand–object interaction datasets are mostly collected in controlled studio settings, limiting environmental diversity and causing poor model generalization to real-world egocentric scenarios.
method: Marker-less multi-camera wearable/portable rig that enables near-unconstrained mobility for capture in natural environments.
Multi-view reconstruction and calibration pipeline combining geometric optimization with learned priors to recover 3D hand poses and object geometry without markers.
Automatic annotation and quality filtering to produce a diverse dataset of synchronized multi-view images and 3D hand/object poses for training and evaluation.
impact: Provides practitioners with a diverse, in-the-wild 3D hand–object dataset and capture methodology that improves model robustness and generalization for applications like AR/VR, egocentric perception, and manipulation in robotics.
visual_elements: Photo of the wearable/multi-camera capture rig worn in everyday environments (street, kitchen, office).
Side-by-side multi-view input images and the resulting 3D reconstruction (hand + object) to show fidelity.
Pipeline flowchart: capture → multi-view calibration → 3D reconstruction → annotation.
Dataset diversity infographic: environment types, number of sessions, distribution of object categories and poses.
paper_title: SHOW3D: Capturing Scenes of 3D Hands and Objects in the Wild
paper_authors: Patrick Rim, Kevin Harris, Braden Copple, Shangchen Han, Xu Xie
